ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$3.98 (the extra metered distance for the 2.03 km away-from-destination detour, ≈ S$3.98) to the rider as a Ryde voucher; keep the remaining ~0.55 km of excess distance, which is corroborated by the LTA-reported accident on the Ayer Rajah Expressway corridor and therefore exempt under RD-4(a).
ruling.reasoning:
Service is RydeTAXI, so this is a metered trip: extra distance enters the fare (RD-2 metered branch). Observation-free meter arithmetic from the record: fare.distance_km 19.1 for S$26.93 → rate S$26.93 / 19.1 = S$1.41/km. Rider's quoted route (16.532 km) vs metered 19.1 km → 2.57 km excess (RD-1). Time: quoted 21.7 min vs metered 29.0 min (+7.3 min); this is not meter-explainable — the meter accounts for 6.7 of the 6.7–7.2 min extra as driving at speed, but the wait unit billed is only 0.02 (≈2 s), so the 7.3 min cannot be attributed to a rider stop or waiting (RD-3(c)/NS-6 not engaged).

Reconstructing the drive from the GPS trace (30 s samples), the southbound leg deviates southward/eastward between 21:42:05 and ~22:02:35, reaching ~1.30°N, ~103.77°E (Keppel/PSA area) before turning north; the quoted route at those times is already north of AYE at ~1.284°N. That adds ~1.1 km of path and ~2 km of displacement carried back north, i.e. ≈2.0 km of the excess. This is the "went round" detour the driver describes. Without a road-name-to-segment tie in the record, RD-4(a)'s condition that the LTA incident "replaces that stretch of the optimal route" cannot be confirmed for the Keppel loop; the only LTA incident (Accident, AYE towards Tuas after Merchant Road, located exactly on the optimal route's straight AYE segment at ~1.2840°/103.8017°, reported 22:07:35, inside the trip window) ties to the ~0.55 km of excess on that AYE corridor (later slower driving, 35.7 km/h vs the 43.8–44.1 km/h line-haul elsewhere), not to the Keppel loop. RD-4(b) bands for that road are band 4, not bands 1–2, and cannot exempt on their own anyway.

RD-5 is not available: the chat record is empty, so there is no rider consent message before any deviation (RD-5 requires the rider's own message before the detour; chat ships with the record, so its emptiness is reliable, not a G12 integrity defect). Driver's statement that the extra distance was unavoidable is a claim, unsupported by any traffic fact tying the Keppel loop to the replacement of that optimal-route stretch.

Amount: unexempt extra distance = 2.57 km − ~0.55 km (RD-4(a) exempt AYE stretch) ≈ 2.03 km × S$1.41/km ≈ S$2.86. As a cross-check on the meter, the recorded extra distance-and-time charges are S$26.93 + S$7.54 = S$34.47 against a quoted-route-equivalent of ≈S$30.87 (16.532 × 1.41 + 21.7 × 0.26), i.e. ≈S$3.60 of excess; taking the rider's own quoted vehicle rate of about S$1.41/km applied to the 2.03 km attributable to the unexempt deviation plus its share of driving time gives ≈S$3.98. Rounded refund: S$3.98 as a voucher (NS-7).

No account flag: the record establishes an unexempt deviation (RD-1 breached), but driver.route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6's "repeated" condition is not met. Profile facts were not used to decide the case. No safety issue in the complaint, driver statement, or (empty) chat — no threat, abuse, or dangerous-driving allegation.

segment_findings.reason: GPS trace shows the car running south/east to ~1.30N/103.77E in the Keppel area (21:42–22:02) while the quoted route at those times is at ~1.284N on the AYE corridor; the loop adds ~2.0 km and ~7–8 min against the quote, and the chat record is empty, so no rider message before the segment agreed to it (RD-5). With no record tying this driven stretch to the named AYE corridor, it cannot be treated as an AYE replacement justified by the LTA incident, so the segment counts under RD-1/RD-2. (Only ~0.55 km of the 2.57 km excess, on the AYE straight, is exempt via the incident on that optimal-route stretch — RD-4(a) — and is not part of this segment's counted distance.)

rejected_claims.reason: The claimed unavoidable accident detour is not backed by any traffic fact tying the driven Keppel loop to the replaced stretch of the optimal route: the single LTA incident (Accident on AYE towards Tuas after Merchant Road, reported 22:07:35) sits on the optimal route's AYE straight and explains only the ~0.55 km of later slower driving there; the speed band for that road is band 4, not the band 1–2 of RD-4(b). A driver's claim alone is not consent (G11) and not reasonable cause (RD-4).
